evals.name: go-native-reply
evals.prompt: Our Go service only needs a typed in-process reply. Show what evidence would admit that surface and what it would not prove.
evals.expected_output: A released Go module, native registration and pipeline test, with a bounded claim.
assertions: Names github.com/cratis/arc.go and resolves its version.
Uses a consuming Go test with an actually dispatched command and inspects success, presence and typed value.
Does not infer HTTP, persistence or authorization from an in-process reply.

evals.name: unproved-elixir-graph
evals.prompt: We have a .NET graph generator example and an Elixir repo listed in the docs. Give us the Elixir graph and proxy implementation.
evals.expected_output: Refuse the unsupported translation and request target-owned evidence.
assertions: Distinguishes repository existence from a released generator contract.
Requests the Elixir declaration and a native consuming generator test.
Does not invent a module or call .NET generation an Elixir result.
Separates emitted graph, proxy compilation and host invocation.

evals.name: java-discovery
evals.prompt: A Kotlin test passed for an asynchronous query. Can our Java Spring service claim the same behavior?
evals.expected_output: A Java-callable signature and Java-side registration/discovery and consumer result are required.
assertions: Requires a Java consumer and verifies the actual asynchronous return contract.
Does not use the Kotlin-only test as proof of Java discovery.
